newsitem.title: FRANCE: French government, striking doctors call for talks.
newsitem.headline: French government, striking doctors call for talks.

text.p: A strike by French junior hospital doctors against government plans to curb health spending went into its fourth week on Monday with both sides calling for serious talks to end the protest.
Social Affairs Minister Barrot met some striking doctors as he visited the Loire valley town of Tours and told them he did not want the dispute to drag on.
He said on Sunday he was ready to resume talks this week but only if negotiations were "serious."

The dispute is losing steam as strikers feel the financial pinch but has hit virtually all of the country's 26 teaching hospitals and is testing the government's resolve to cut state budget deficits so that France can qualify for the European Union's single currency.
The head of the junior doctors union, Gilbert Zakine, said they were determined to carry on with the protest but would negotiate provided the government had a satisfactory proposal.
Barrot, accusing the strikers of promoting their own sectional interests, has refused demands to scrap or delay plans to fine all doctors in regions that overshoot state spending limits.
To try appease them, he said doctors' fees could increase if spending was kept under target. But he said that the government would get tougher if the strike continued.
The strikers, who blocked some roads and railways last week, said they were preparing more, unspecified disruption. They called for a demonstration in Paris on April 13.
